title.value: An Intentional Forgetting-Driven Self-Healing Method For Deep Reinforcement Learning Systems
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the core topic of the paper which introduces a method for self-healing in deep reinforcement learning systems using intentional forgetting.
title.quote: An Intentional Forgetting-Driven Self-Healing Method For Deep Reinforcement Learning Systems

extractions.description: The paper presents a novel approach called Dr. DRL, which uses intentional forgetting to improve the self-healing capabilities of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) systems in the face of environmental drifts. The method enhances the continual learning process by prioritizing the adaptation of key problem-solving skills while discarding less critical behaviors. The evaluation shows improvements in cost-efficiency, adaptability, and rewards compared to traditional continual learning.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on improving the adaptability and efficiency of DRL systems in general software environments, which may support various applications but does not specifically target climate or ecologically-related sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is increasingly applied in large-scale productions like Netflix and Facebook.

primary_category.justification: The focus of the paper is on improving software systems through deep reinforcement learning technology without direct emphasis on climate or ecological topics.
primary_category.quote: ...propose Dr. DRL, a self-healing approach for DRL that leverages intentional forgetting combined with continual learning in order to optimize the agent’s plasticity and accelerate its adaptation to drifted environments.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes related to climate or ecological factors within the paper.
secondary_categories.quote: As with most data-driven systems, DRL systems can exhibit undesirable behaviors due to environmental drifts, which often occur in constantly-changing production settings.

primary_sub_category.justification: No specific sub-categories align with the content of the paper as it does not directly engage with climate or ecological aspects.
primary_sub_category.quote: The burgeoning field of ML (and RL) operations (MLOps) (and RLOps) is establishing the best practices and methods for implementing efficient, trustworthy, and maintainable self-learning systems.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not address secondary climate or ecological sub-categories but instead focuses on general improvements to DRL systems.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Continual Learning (CL) is the inherent self-healing approach for adapting the DRL agent in response to the environment’s conditions shifts.

applications.value: Improving adaptability and efficiency of DRL systems in software environments.
applications.justification: The paper focuses on enhancing the adaptability and resilience of DRL systems through a new self-healing method, which can have applications across various industries using DRL.
applications.quote: Dr. DRL is compared with vanilla CL on various drifted environments. Dr. DRL is able to reduce, on average, the healing time and fine-tuning episodes by, respectively, 18.74% and 17.72%.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper effectively falls under general advancements in machine learning and software systems rather than necessitating a new category related to sustainability.
new_primary_category.quote: The paper focuses on improvements to reinforcement learning systems, rather than specific ecological or climate-related applications.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category is needed as the contributions are primarily within the domain of DRL and continual learning processes.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our proposed method to properly forget the minor behaviors involves the re-initialization of their associated neurons using the original weight initializer.
